title: Round 11 - fix 4, and a measurement defect caught by a failed prediction
focus: Implement the recommendation open since round 6: score the live desk's own record, split into contiguous sub-periods, and weight it above the backtest matrices as a ranking input rather than only a liveness floor.
headline: The first attempt at the live matrix was invalid - six independent sub-window runs forced every card to liquidate and re-enter, biasing results toward high-turnover cards - and it was only caught because it produced the seat a pre-registered prediction said should not win; the rebuilt, cumulative version then reversed round 8's override and vindicated round 10's.
outcome:
The plan pre-registered cutting the live period into six sub-windows, but the first implementation ran each as its own independent tournament, so a card that entered in March and held into August was forced to liquidate and re-enter at every boundary. B-momentum showed zero trades and zero exposure in two entire sub-windows on this broken matrix even though it was fully invested, and the bias was directional: high-turnover cards barely noticed the reset while hold-and-ride cards were destroyed by it.

The broken matrix also produced the convenient answer, seating A-rotation alone - the same card the owner had overridden round 10's rule to keep one day earlier. What caught it was a pre-committed prediction that B3-concentrated, not A-rotation, should lead the live matrix; the prediction was contradicted, prompting a look at the suspicious zero-percent cells instead of shipping the roster. The defect was logged and the runs were rebuilt as cumulative totals from one fixed start, differenced to recover each sub-period exactly, with no gate or threshold moved by the fix.

On the corrected matrix, three ranked seats resulted: B3-concentrated (momentum), A-rotation (pairs-rotation) and C-trend (trend), with a fourth card eliminated by a gate requiring positive results in at least three of six sub-periods. B-momentum cleared every gate and ranked second on the live matrix, but lost the momentum seat to B3-concentrated on distinctness.

The corrected result split the programme's two prior overrides rather than simply ratifying either: round 8's override, which had preferred B-momentum over B3-concentrated, was reversed by the live evidence, while round 10's override, which had kept A-rotation despite the backtest dispersion gate, was vindicated by it. The document frames this as the most trustworthy outcome available, since a live-first rule that had simply agreed with every prior owner decision would be indistinguishable from one fitted to them.

The desk owner then added B-momentum back as a fifth seat, overriding the distinctness rule rather than the ranking itself, arguing that B-momentum's holdings are a legible superset of B3-concentrated's (a strict four-of-six-name overlap) rather than a duplicate signal.
owner_override: The rule's own ranking seated B3-concentrated, A-rotation and C-trend, dropping B-momentum because it shares a base family with B3-concentrated. The desk owner overrode the distinctness rule (not the rank order, which is unchanged) and added B-momentum back as a fifth seat, on the grounds that its current holdings are a strict superset of B3-concentrated's (four of six names shared, two additional names not held by the narrower card) rather than a redundant duplicate of the same idea.
carries_forward: Fix 4 should not be treated as finished - the live matrix is one environment and only time makes it multi-regime, so backtest matrices should keep being reported beside it as floors and a tie-break, not discarded.

The B-variant tie (B-momentum, B4-tight-stop, B2-hold-90 posting near-identical live cells across five of six sub-periods) is a real measurement gap needing a window where a stop-loss or holding cap actually fires, not a scoring fix.

Distinctness needs re-specifying over what a card actually holds rather than its base-family lineage, since the B3-concentrated/B-momentum pairing shows family-based distinctness can wrongly exclude a genuinely informative comparison.

D5 (independent sub-window runs resetting position continuity) is a class of error, not a one-off - any future matrix built by slicing a live period must preserve continuity across the slices via cumulative-and-difference, not independent runs.
